summary: Sacks argues that despite missing consumer user and revenue targets, OpenAI's strong GPT-5.5 product release, new base model (Spud), and compute advantage over Anthropic position it well to win the all-important enterprise/coding market, making Sam's big compute bet likely to pay off for the right reasons.
quote: I think Sam may end up being right here for the wrong reason, which is he missed on consumer, but enterprise is going gangbusters and is giving him the ability now, I think, to catch up on consumer.

summary: Chamath believes OpenAI's missed targets reflect a supply-side power/compute constraint rather than weak demand, and that the company is on track to be a multi-trillion-dollar business; the real risk is losing compute access to hyperscalers.
quote: I think they're going to be fine. I think this is a multi-trillion-dollar company... To the extent that OpenAI missed, I think what that is is an insight to not enough compute capacity today.

summary: Sacks argues Anthropic is being hurt by being token/compute constrained, which is causing it to gate Opus 4.7 with reduced thinking time, drawing complaints and developer defections to GPT-5.5, weakening its competitive position in the critical coding market.
quote: Anthropic is token constrained. It's reducing their ability to serve Mythos, for example. It's causing them to engage in compute gating with Opus 4.7.

summary: Chamath believes Anthropic, like OpenAI, is a multi-trillion-dollar company whose apparent misses are purely supply-side power constraints, not demand weakness, and that it will continue to grow as compute access expands.
quote: I think Anthropic is a multi-trillion-dollar company. I think the thing that's happening right now is a complete misunderstanding of what's actually happening inside of the world of AI.

summary: Sacks credits Google's remarkable comeback with Gemini — Sergey's return, integration into Search, and strong cloud growth — as the key reason OpenAI missed consumer targets, positioning Google as a major winner in both consumer AI and enterprise cloud.
quote: If there is a single reason why OpenAI did not hit its user targets and its revenue targets, certainly around consumer, you'd have to say it's because Google managed to take meaningful share.
